children: Tesla Inc.
will add an extra production shift to finish outstanding Cybertruck orders before it dismantles the line next year.
On Saturday, CEO
Elon Musk
said in a post on X that the backlog is "far more than Tesla can make" before the line comes down around June or July next year. "We will add an extra shift to try to get all orders done in time."
The Tesla Cybertruck order backlog is currently far more than we can make before dismantling the line for Cybercab expansion around June/July next year.
We will add an extra shift to try to get all orders done in time.
Cybercab Takes Priority in Tesla’s AI Pivot
Musk said a day earlier that Tesla would
at its Texas factory and shift resources toward the Cybercab, a two-seat robotaxi, according to Reuters.
The Cybercab plays a key role in Musk’s plan to transform Tesla from an automaker into a company focused on AI and robotics.
Musk’s latest comments follow criticism from investor
Ross Gerber
, CEO of
Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management
, who called the wind-down "another failure" in a post on X. Fellow investor
Gary Black
wrote on X that Tesla missed an opportunity by not building a more conventional-looking pickup.
Cybertruck Sales Run Far Below Musk’s Target
The Cybertruck began reaching customers in late 2023 but has struggled to meet Musk’s early expectations.
Tesla’s "other models" category, which includes the Cybertruck, totaled
, according to a Benzinga analysis of the company’s data. That is the most Cybertrucks Tesla could have sold in the period.
The figure implies annualized sales of 28,000 to 32,000 units. At the high end, that is about 13% of Musk’s 250,000 annual goal.
The stainless steel pickup has also faced repeated recalls and quality concerns since launch. Its unconventional design limited prospects in overseas markets,
The Texas-based automobile and energy technology company has a market capitalization of about $1.42 trillion. Over the past 52 weeks, its stock has traded as high as $498.83 and as low as $297.38.
